brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Hex base pieces piece:0,0,0 (full) and piece:0,-1,0 (full) and piece:1,0,0 (half-e). Removable bins sit in the cells: bin:0,0,0 (full depth, 3 compartments) and bin:0,-1,0 (full depth, 2 compartments). They drop in and hang on their rims, so they lift out.

Notch drawer frame notch:0#1,-1#notch3 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) fills the empty position at (1,-1) between the bases. A drawer could not be placed on a half base's cut face, so the notch drawer was used instead.
handle:0,-1,0;top on the cover cover:0,-1,0;full;top, with inserts. Added via addHandle on the top cover.
The build is a compact cluster of about 3 cells with a top handle, but the configurator does not check weight or portability; the handle and print material are not verified.
Compartmented bins suit small parts. No props were added because the brief is about structure, not staging.

finish.summary: Built a small portable organizer: three hex base cells (full at 0,0 and 0,-1, half-east at 1,0), two removable bins (3-compartment at 0,0 and 2-compartment at 0,-1), a notch drawer frame at 1,-1, a top carry handle on the cover at 0,-1, and all open faces capped with joints locked. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. Limitations: the configurator cannot verify weight, material, or drawer contents; the drawer is a frame-type notch rather than a half-base drawer, since drawers on a half base's cut face were not offered.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
